The geological drama and the contrast between barren new lava and thriving colonised rock makes this one of the Azores' most unusual and memorable dives.
getThere: This remote bank lies between Terceira and São Miguel and is accessed by liveaboard from Horta or Angra do Heroísmo. It is not accessible on a day trip from any single island; dedicated liveaboard itineraries visit it as part of a multi-island circuit. Flying into Horta or Terceira airports is the usual approach.

name: Playa Chica
description: Playa Chica is Lanzarote's premier shore dive, located directly off the beach at Puerto del Carmen and accessible by finning from the shore. A shallow volcanic reef at 5 to 8 m gives way to a sandy rubble slope dropping to a 20 m plateau and then to a 28 m drop-off. Angel sharks (Squatina squatina) rest motionless on the sand during daylight hours and are almost guaranteed on winter and spring dives when Atlantic upwelling cools the water. Stingrays, guitarfish, and common octopus are equally reliable. In the shallows, posidonia seagrass patches host pipefish and juvenile wrasse. Night dives reveal active hunting by moray eels, cuttlefish, and mantis shrimp. This site is good for all levels and is one of the most consistently species-rich dives in the Canary Islands.
getThere: Shore dive from Playa Chica beach in Puerto del Carmen, the main resort town on Lanzarote's east coast. Arrecife airport is 15 minutes by car. Multiple dive centres operate from the beach promenade and rent equipment; the entry point is a concrete ramp on the north end of the beach.

name: West Channel
description: The West Channel is the main tidal passage connecting Aldabra's vast lagoon to the open Indian Ocean, and it produces some of the most exhilarating drift diving in the western Indian Ocean. As tides flush through the narrow cut, nutrient-rich water attracts enormous schools of fusiliers, snappers, and jacks that in turn bring hammerhead sharks, bull sharks, and eagle rays. The channel walls are encrusted with rich soft coral and large sea fans angled into the flow. Timing is everything here — the optimal window is the outgoing tide when visibility peaks and the current runs fast enough to cover the full channel in a single drift.
getThere: Aldabra is accessible only by liveaboard expedition vessel departing from Mahé or Praslin in the Seychelles, with voyage durations of 10 to 14 days. The Seychelles Islands Foundation manages all access permits.

name: Grand Passage
description: Grand Passage on Aldabra's northern rim is the widest and deepest of the atoll's tidal channels, broad enough for large vessels to transit and deep enough that its walls host communities more typical of open-ocean reef than shallow atoll. Manta rays are regular visitors feeding on the concentrated plankton the passage produces, and whale sharks are seen here between October and December. The walls are festooned with gorgonian fans and black coral trees below 20 metres, and large schools of humpback snapper and dogtooth tuna hold station in the mid-water column. This is a site for experienced divers comfortable managing currents that can run at several knots.
getThere: Grand Passage is reached by liveaboard expedition from the Seychelles. All visits require prior permit approval from the Seychelles Islands Foundation.

name: Turtle Rock Wall
description: Turtle Rock is a limestone pinnacle on Aldabra's southern outer reef where a vertical wall drops from 3 metres to 40 metres and beyond. The site takes its name from the extraordinary density of green turtles that rest in crevices and graze on the algae covering the rock face — sightings of a dozen or more turtles in a single dive are routine. The wall itself is a tapestry of hard coral, tube sponge, and large barrel sponge, with hawksbill turtles joining their green cousins at the cleaning stations. Below 25 metres the reef transitions to a rubble slope where whitetip reef sharks rest in loose groups, and the occasional tiger shark has been documented cruising the base.
getThere: Turtle Rock is dived from liveaboard tenders during permitted Aldabra expeditions departing the Seychelles.

name: Passe Houareau
description: Passe Houareau on Aldabra's southeastern rim is the atoll's shallowest and most sheltered passage, making it the most approachable for divers less experienced with strong tidal flow. The channel floor is a mosaic of hard coral gardens interspersed with sand patches, with butterflyfish, angelfish, and triggerfish in dense reef communities on either side. The site is one of the best inside Aldabra for macro life: nudibranchs, flatworms, and mantis shrimp are found throughout the coral rubble, and the seagrass beds at the lagoon mouth support green turtles feeding throughout the day. On incoming tides, juvenile sharks use the passage as a nursery, and the concentration of small fish brings hunting trevally and the occasional reef octopus.
getThere: Passe Houareau is reached by liveaboard tender during permitted Aldabra expeditions. Seychelles Islands Foundation permit required for all visits.

name: Wall Street
description: Wall Street is the signature reef wall dive on Providenciales, dropping vertically from 15 metres to beyond recreational limits along the edge of the Caicos Bank. Spur and groove formations at the top transition abruptly into a sheer coral face draped with sea fans and black coral at depth. Caribbean reef sharks patrol the wall edge consistently, and the occasional passing hawksbill turtle is common. Current can accelerate along the wall during tidal exchanges, creating ideal conditions for drift diving and pelagic encounters.
getThere: Boat dive departing from Turtle Cove Marina on Providenciales. Most operators run two-tank morning trips to the wall, approximately 20 minutes by boat from the marina.

name: The Crack
description: The Crack is a dramatic fissure in the reef platform on the Northwest Point wall system, where the coral plateau splits open and divers can swim down through a canyon that opens onto the main wall face. The crevice itself is densely packed with glassy sweepers and copper sweepers that catch the light in shimmering curtains. Nurse sharks rest on the sandy floor of the canyon, and lobster occupy every overhang. The exit onto the open wall brings an abrupt shift to big water, with reef sharks visible in the blue water column below.
getThere: Boat dive from Turtle Cove Marina, Providenciales. The site is on the Northwest Point wall system, approximately 25 minutes by boat.

name: Shark Hotel
description: Shark Hotel is a cleaning station on the Northwest Point wall where Caribbean reef sharks reliably gather in numbers that make it one of the most reliable shark dives in the Atlantic. At the cleaning station at around 20 metres, five to fifteen reef sharks at a time circle the coral heads while cleaner wrasse tend to them. The site earns its name from the regularity of the aggregation — divers kneel on sand patches and watch the sharks move in slow arcs overhead. Blacktip sharks occasionally join the gathering, and the wall below hosts large schools of horse-eye jacks.
getThere: Boat dive from Turtle Cove Marina on Providenciales. Northwest Point wall sites are 20 to 25 minutes by boat. Morning departures recommended to catch sharks at the cleaning station.

name: Rock Monster Chimney
description: Rock Monster Chimney is a wall dive on the south side of Cayman Brac featuring a distinctive volcanic chimney formation that divers descend through from 15 metres to exit on the wall at 27 metres. The chimney interior is lined with orange sponges and tube worms, and silversides fill the passage during summer months. Outside on the wall face, black coral trees grow at depth and large barrel sponges anchor the coral landscape. Spotted eagle rays are frequently seen cruising the wall, and the overhang at the chimney base shelters resting nurse sharks.
getThere: Boat dive from the south side of Cayman Brac. Reef Divers at the Brac Reef Beach Resort is the closest operator, approximately 10 minutes by boat.

name: Wilderness Wall
description: Wilderness Wall is on the remote east end of Cayman Brac, rarely dived due to its distance from the main operators and exposure to ocean swell. Those who make the trip are rewarded with pristine coral in an almost undisturbed state — high coral cover, thick sea fan formations, and virtually no diver impact. The wall drops from 15 metres into deep blue water and supports one of the densest black coral communities in the Caymans at depth. Large Nassau grouper in spawning aggregation size are present near the wall edge, and the site is known for consistent sightings of reef sharks well away from any feeding site.
getThere: Long boat ride from operators on the west end of Cayman Brac, 30 to 40 minutes each way. Best accessed on calm days only. Confirm conditions and operator willingness before booking — most skip the east end during winter swells.

name: Inside Out
description: Inside Out is a unique dive on the north wall of Cayman Brac where a large coral archway creates a swim-through from the reef flat into open wall. The tunnel is wide enough for comfortable passage and lit with ambient light from both ends, making it accessible without torch diving skills. The arch itself is heavily colonized with encrusting sponges in reds and purples, and green moray eels occupy the crevices at its base. Exiting onto the wall brings divers face to face with the open Atlantic blue, and nurse sharks are almost always found resting in the sand channels on the reef flat at the tunnel entrance.
getThere: Boat dive from the north shore of Cayman Brac. Brac Aquatics or Reef Divers can reach this site in 10 to 15 minutes.

name: El Ancla (The Anchor)
description: A broad rocky plateau at the southern tip of Wolf Island named for a rusting anchor wedged into basalt at 18 m. The flat shelf funnels the Cromwell Undercurrent into an upwelling that aggregates whale sharks from June through November and draws schools of scalloped hammerheads in numbers regularly exceeding 200 individuals. Galápagos sharks patrol the mid-water column while eagle rays cruise in formation overhead. Surge can be moderate but conditions are calmer than the exposed north face, making this the preferred site when swell exceeds 2 m.
getThere: Reached only by liveaboard from Puerto Ayora or Puerto Baquerizo Moreno; typical crossing 18 to 22 hours.

name: Mola Point
description: The western headland of Wolf Island rises from 40 m and hosts the highest recorded mola mola (ocean sunfish) encounter rates in the Galápagos, particularly from July through October when cool Humboldt water pushes surface temperatures below 20 °C. Mola sunfish gather along the wall at 15 to 30 m depth where marine iguanas and brightly coloured wrasse pick parasites from their flanks — a cleaning station dynamic rarely observed elsewhere. Galápagos sea lions tumble through the blue water above while silky sharks cruise the outer column. Current runs consistently moderate to strong along this exposed face.
getThere: Reached only by liveaboard from Puerto Ayora or Puerto Baquerizo Moreno; typical crossing 18 to 22 hours.

name: Darwin North Wall
description: The sheer north face of Darwin Island drops vertically from the surface to beyond 60 m, its walls encrusted with black coral fans, sponges, and Tubastrea coral in brilliant orange and yellow. This is one of the premier whale shark aggregation sites in the world — resident whale sharks (some exceeding 12 m) patrol 5 to 25 m depth along the wall face during the cool season June through November. Schools of scalloped hammerheads numbering in the hundreds assemble at 20 to 35 m while silky sharks and Galápagos sharks hold the outer column. Current at the north face is typically moderate, easing to mild in the afternoon.
getThere: Darwin Island is accessible only by liveaboard departing Puerto Ayora or Puerto Baquerizo Moreno; transfer time is approximately 24 hours.

name: Hammerhead Highway
description: A submerged ridge extending east from Darwin Island creates a natural funnel for scalloped hammerheads — the tightly packed schools here are among the largest consistently recorded anywhere in the Galápagos, with counts exceeding 300 individuals common during peak season (July through October). The ridge crest at 20 m and the sand channel at 28 m are the focal points; divers drop to depth early and hold position as successive waves of hammerheads sweep overhead. Galápagos sharks and large schools of bigeye jacks fill the mid-water between passes. Current can push hard over the ridge tip.
getThere: Darwin Island is accessible only by liveaboard departing Puerto Ayora or Puerto Baquerizo Moreno; transfer time is approximately 24 hours.

name: Shark Cathedral
description: A dramatic submerged amphitheatre of collapsed basalt columns on Darwin's south flank creates a natural arena at 22 to 38 m. The stacked rock ledges and overhangs shelter white-tip reef sharks resting in groups of 10 to 30 during daylight hours, while the open water above fills with hammerheads and Galápagos sharks. Mola mola appear seasonally (July through October) drifting near the outer lip. The protected geometry of the site dampens current to mild even when the surrounding ocean is running strong, making it a reliable second dive when conditions elsewhere at Darwin are too punishing.
getThere: Darwin Island is accessible only by liveaboard departing Puerto Ayora or Puerto Baquerizo Moreno; transfer time is approximately 24 hours.

name: Stiniva Cave
description: A large sea cave on Vis's southeastern shore penetrates 60 m into the limestone cliff, with the ceiling dropping to a tight 4 m sump at the back that opens into an air pocket. The entrance walls are plastered with yellow and orange encrusting sponges, purple sea fans, and red coral fragments (Corallium rubrum). Large moray eels rest in wall crevices throughout, and a resident group of common dentex patrols the entrance zone. One of the Adriatic's finest cavern dives.
getThere: Ferry from Split to Vis Town (2.5 hours) or fast catamaran (1 hour). Dive centres in Vis Town and Komiza run boat charters to Stiniva; by road Stiniva cove is reached by a steep track from the main island road.

name: Monk Seal Wall
description: A dramatic vertical limestone wall on Vis's northwestern tip drops from 2 m to over 50 m and takes its name from the Mediterranean monk seals that historically pup in the adjacent sea caves — occasional encounters still occur. The upper section hosts dense posidonia seagrass and saddled bream, the mid-wall is covered in red corallium and yellow tube sponges, and deeper sections yield large grouper and enormous conger eels. Rare Adriatic nudibranchs including Flabellina affinis and Hypselodoris valenciennesi appear on the gorgonian fans in summer.
getThere: Ferry from Split to Vis Town, then boat charter from Komiza on the western side of the island. The wall is a 15 minute boat ride from Komiza harbour.

name: Bisevo Wall
description: The eastern wall of the tiny island of Bisevo just south of Vis drops sheer from the waterline to 40 m and is one of the most biologically rich walls in the central Adriatic. Giant grouper up to 30 kg lurk in the overhangs, enormous schools of saddled bream and two-banded bream sweep the mid-water column, and Mediterranean moray eels reach exceptional sizes here. The wall's inaccessibility — Bisevo has no permanent facilities — keeps diver pressure minimal and marine life correspondingly bold.
getThere: Day trips depart from Komiza on Vis's western coast; the crossing to Bisevo takes approximately 30 minutes. Bisevo is best visited in calm summer conditions as the island offers no shelter from westerly swells.

name: Ravnik Green Cave
description: The Green Cave (Zelena spilja) on the islet of Ravnik south of Vis is entered by swimming through a partially submerged entrance tunnel at around 1.5 m depth. Inside, sunlight refracts through an underwater window in the cave floor from about 11 m depth, filling the cavern with an extraordinary emerald glow during late morning hours. The walls are encrusted with Mediterranean sponges and small sea anemones, and common octopus are reliably found in every crevice. Nudibranchs — especially Cratena peregrina on the cave mouth hydroids — are an outstanding macro subject.
getThere: Boat charter from Komiza on Vis Island; Ravnik islet is a 20 minute ride. Best visited at 10 to 11 am when the sun angle creates the full green light effect inside the cave.

name: Barracuda Point
description: The northwest tip of Gili Trawangan where a reef promontory channels the Lombok Strait current into an accelerated flow that concentrates schooling fish in numbers unseen at the calmer inshore sites. A resident school of great barracuda — typically 50 to 100 individuals — hovers mid-water in the current at 12 to 20 metres, holding station in a slowly rotating tornado formation that is one of the most photographed spectacles in the Gilis. Blacktip and whitetip reef sharks appear on most dives, hunting the edges of the school, while giant trevally patrol from below. The coral slope drops to 30 metres with dense sea fans and large barrel sponges, and the current — when running — creates an effortless drift finish back toward the boat.
getThere: Boat dive from Gili Trawangan harbour. Most dive operators on Gili T run morning and afternoon trips to Barracuda Point — the crossing takes 5 to 10 minutes.

name: East Coast Wall
description: Pemba's exposed eastern coastline takes the full force of Indian Ocean swells and in return hosts some of the archipelago's most dramatic vertical walls, dropping from the reef flat at 8 m to beyond 800 m into the Pemba Channel. The upper wall to 30 m is plastered in golden gorgonians and black coral trees that grow laterally in the current, each colony hosting its own community of pygmy hawkfish, longnose hawkfish, and clingfish. Schooling barracuda — sometimes in aggregations of several hundred — spiral in midwater just off the wall edge, and pelagics including dog-tooth tuna and wahoo hunt beneath the school. The current can be significant on incoming tide so this site is reserved for experienced divers who can hold their depth at the wall face without being swept into blue water.
getThere: Accessed by liveaboard or from Fundu Lagoon resort on Pemba's west coast via a 25 minute boat transfer around the southern tip. The east coast is exposed and only accessible in calm weather; operators typically schedule east coast dives in the June to October southeast monsoon window when swells are lower.

name: Poblacion Muck
description: Poblacion is a shore-entry muck site directly in front of Dauin town proper, where the volcanic black sand slopes gradually from knee depth to around 22 metres and concentrates a rotating cast of rare critters that keeps macro photographers returning dive after dive. Frogfish in improbable colour morphs — bright pink, algae-covered, pure white — wedge themselves among coral rubble, while mimic octopus emerge from burrows and cycle through their repertoire of flounder, lionfish, and banded sea snake imitations. Ghost pipefish in ornate and robust forms drift alongside crinoids in the 12 to 18 metre range, and tiger mantis shrimp patrol the open sand between rubble patches.
getThere: Poblacion is a shore-entry site fronting Dauin town centre, 20 km south of Dumaguete City by jeepney or tricycle. Most Dauin dive resorts organise guided shore dives here and include it in their house-reef programme.

name: Bonnet Reef
description: Bonnet Reef sits a short banca ride off the Dauin coast and marks a transition from the area's trademark muck habitats into a proper coral reef ecosystem, with a rubble slope giving way to hard coral terraces and then a clean sandy plain at depth that still concentrates muck life alongside reef species. The upper reef is dense with anthias clouds, schooling fusiliers, and resident groups of bumphead parrotfish that make grinding passes over coral heads at dawn, while the deeper sand at 25 to 35 metres is a reliable location for hairy frogfish and Ambon scorpionfish — a master of dead-leaf disguise. Ghost pipefish hover at the reef-sand interface, making this one of the few sites around Dauin where a single dive yields both reef and muck photography.
getThere: Bonnet Reef is a 10-minute banca ride from Dauin shore. Dauin-based dive operators include it in their standard boat-dive schedule; dedicated guided trips can be arranged for photographers who want an early-morning bumphead parrotfish encounter.

name: Mainit Muck
description: Mainit — meaning 'hot' in Visayan — takes its name from geothermal vents that bubble warm sulphurous water through the black sand at depth, creating a unique microenvironment that attracts critters rarely found in the more famous Dauin sites to the north. The vent areas at 18 to 28 metres support unusual colour morphs of frogfish and scorpionfish apparently drawn by the warmer substrate, and the site is one of the most reliable locations in the Philippines for the elusive Sargassum ghost pipefish, which drifts in loose mimicry of floating weed fragments in the 15 to 20 metre zone. The shallower rubble terrace concentrates flamboyant cuttlefish, wonderpus octopus, and endemic Bargibant's pygmy seahorses on scattered sea fans, making Mainit a top pick for macro photographers seeking rarer
getThere: Mainit is a 15-minute banca ride south from Dauin, located near Malatapay on the Negros Oriental coast. Dive operators in Dauin schedule regular boat trips; the site is also accessible from operators based at Apo Island resorts as a return-leg dive.

name: San Miguel Slope
description: San Miguel Slope lies north of Dumaguete City in the barangay of San Miguel, where a long gentle volcanic sand and rubble slope descends from very shallow water to 30 metres and intercepts open-water currents that push in from the Tañon Strait. The combination of nutrient-rich water and complex mixed substrate makes it a strong bet for deep muck rarities — coconut octopus burying themselves with paired shell halves, robust ghost pipefish in multiple colour morphs hovering at hydroid clusters, and hairy frogfish in slow-walk hunting mode across the sand. The moderate current in the 15 to 25 metre zone concentrates longnose hawkfish on sea fans and brings in open-water pelagics like rainbow runners that cruise the slope edge, giving San Miguel a dual character as both muck site and drift
getThere: San Miguel Slope is 8 km north of Dumaguete City centre, accessible by tricycle from town or from Sibulan Airport. A handful of dive operators based in Dumaguete City run day trips; it is most commonly accessed as a drift dive on incoming tides when current is running.

name: Boo Islands
description: A cluster of mushroom-shaped karst islets west of Misool whose underwater foundations plunge into cathedral walls encrusted from 3 m to 40 m with some of the densest soft-coral growth in Raja Ampat. The signature dive is Boo Rock, a submerged pinnacle fully draped in pink and orange Dendronephthya; tidal surges push plankton-rich water against the wall, drawing pygmy seahorses on sea fans, ornate ghost pipefish hovering in the current, and large schools of batfish circling the summit. Wobbegong sharks wedge into crevices at the base. Visibility regularly exceeds 25 m on incoming tide.
getThere: Liveaboard from Sorong (3 to 4 hour steam south); day trips not available from shore.

name: Fam Islands
description: A remote island group northwest of Sorong inside the Bird's Head Seascape with almost no permanent dive infrastructure, keeping fish populations and hard coral cover at near-pristine levels. Shallow plateaus at 5 to 12 m hold the highest documented branching Acropora table coral densities in the region; below 20 m, walls open into blue water patrolled by dogtooth tuna and grey reef sharks. Because few liveaboards include Fam in their itineraries, even heavily-trafficked species such as bumphead parrotfish show little diver-avoidance behaviour. Dawn light through the karst silhouettes makes for exceptional wide-angle photography.
getThere: Liveaboard from Sorong; the island group is roughly 2 hours northwest of Sorong by fast boat.

name: Wayag Northern Pinnacles
description: The northernmost reef structures of the Wayag atoll system, reached only by liveaboard after a 5 to 6 hour crossing from Sorong. Submerged limestone pinnacles rise from 35 m to within a metre of the surface; each column is smothered in pristine hard coral untouched by anchor damage. Current converges from three directions at the pinnacle tips, aggregating huge schools of sweetlips, batfish, and Spanish mackerel above, while below 20 m grey reef sharks and silvertip sharks cruise the bases. Because Wayag sits inside a strictly managed marine protected area, the hard coral cover here represents some of the highest in the entire Coral Triangle. Macro life — pygmy seahorses, ponytail nudibranchs, and ornate ghost pipefish — hides in the sea fans on the sheltered east faces.
getThere: Liveaboard from Sorong only; Wayag is 5 to 6 hours northwest by boat. Day trips are not practical.

name: Kawe Island Reef
description: The northern fringe of Kawe Island in the Wayag subdistrict holds a broad shallow shelf, 8 to 18 m, blanketed in branching and tabulate Acropora that ranks among the least disturbed hard coral gardens in Indonesia. Occasional strong upwellings from the deep Halmahera Sea keep temperatures slightly cooler than the Dampier Strait, which suppresses bleaching and feeds dense fish communities. Titan triggerfish, Napolean wrasse, and reef octopus are common on the flat; descending the fore-reef slope reveals large gorgonian sea fans and regular sightings of the rarely-encountered tasselled wobbegong at depth. Almost no dive operators currently visit; access requires a northern Wayag liveaboard itinerary.
getThere: Northern liveaboard itinerary from Sorong only; combine with Wayag. No shore access or resort dives available.

name: Minamijima Arch
description: Minamijima — a restricted uninhabited island at the southern tip of the Ogasawara chain accessible only by permit on licensed tour boats — hosts one of the Pacific's most dramatic volcanic arches at 18 m. The arch spans roughly 20 m and frames a curtain of golden anthias over hard coral terraces carpeted in tabletop Acropora. Visibility regularly exceeds 40 m in summer. Green turtles rest on ledges above the arch; white-tip reef sharks patrol the sandy channel below. The wrought-iron butterflyfish (Chaetodon daedalma), endemic to the southern Izu and Ogasawara islands, appears in small groups on the deeper coral slopes. Light penetration through the arch at midday creates exceptional photography conditions.
getThere: Minamijima is a protected restricted island accessible only on licensed day tours departing Futami Port on Chichijima. Reach Chichijima via the Ogasawara Maru ferry from Takeshiba Pier, Tokyo — a single weekly sailing of approximately 25 hours each way. Book tour boats through operators on Chichijima; permits for Minamijima are arranged by the operator.

name: South Chichijima Wall
description: The southern coastline of Chichijima drops away in a sheer wall from 8 m to beyond 40 m, studded with black coral trees, large sea fans, and colonies of cup coral that thrive in the nutrient-rich upwelling. This is one of the most accessible advanced dive sites in Ogasawara — reachable by day boat in under 20 minutes from Futami Port. Hawksbill turtles forage on the sponge-encrusted wall face, and schools of yellowfin goatfish and dogtooth tuna frequent the blue water at the wall's edge. In summer, pelagic visitors including oceanic whitetip sharks and occasional sperm whale clicks (audible through the water column) elevate the dives. The wall's sheer profile with frequent overhangs creates micro-habitats for shy species including scorpionfish and moray eels.
getThere: Day boats depart Futami Port on Chichijima; the south wall sites are 15 to 20 minutes by boat. Reach Chichijima via the Ogasawara Maru ferry from Takeshiba Pier in Tokyo — approximately 25 hours, running roughly once weekly. Book dive operators on the island in advance.

name: Hahajima Hammerhead Point
description: Hahajima, the second-largest island in the Ogasawara group, is accessed by a smaller inter-island ferry from Chichijima and offers the best hammerhead shark diving in Japan. A seamount off the island's northern tip concentrates scalloped hammerheads (Sphyrna lewini) from June through September in aggregations that can reach 50 to 100 individuals on productive days. The cleaning station dynamics at 25 to 35 m draw the sharks in vertical columns; divers kneel on the sandy plateau and wait as the sharks spiral overhead. Oceanic blacktip sharks, silvertip sharks, and occasional tiger sharks add to the pelagic show. Outside hammerhead season the site produces large pelagic fish, resident sea turtles, and the dramatic deep wall that characterises Ogasawara's underwater topography.
getThere: Reach Hahajima via the Hahajima Maru inter-island ferry from Futami Port on Chichijima — approximately 2 hours each way, running several times weekly. Chichijima itself is reached on the Ogasawara Maru from Takeshiba Pier, Tokyo (approximately 25 hours). Dive operators on Hahajima run day boats to the hammerhead point; advance booking essential in peak season June through September.

name: Chichijima Dolphin Reef
description: The sheltered bays and reef systems on Chichijima's western coast form the primary habitat for resident pods of Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops aduncus) and spinner dolphins (Stenella longirostris). Unlike snorkel-only dolphin swim tours, this site combines scuba diving on the shallow reef with frequent dolphin encounters — the pods regularly investigate divers ascending the reef slope at 8 to 15 m. The reef itself hosts the wrought-iron butterflyfish (Chaetodon daedalma), endemic to the Ogasawara and southern Izu Islands, in concentrations unusual even within their limited range. Sperm whales (Physeter macrocephalus) are heard and occasionally seen in the open water column outside the reef from June through October.
getThere: Day boats depart Futami Port on Chichijima; western bay reef sites are 10 to 30 minutes by boat. Reach Chichijima via the Ogasawara Maru ferry from Takeshiba Pier, Tokyo (approximately 25 hours, roughly once weekly). Local dive operators manage permitting for protected reef areas; advance booking recommended.

name: Motu Nui
description: The outermost of the three small islets off the southwestern tip of Rapa Nui, Motu Nui was the sacred destination of the annual Birdman ceremony and underwater it is equally dramatic. Sheer basalt walls plunge into the open Pacific, patrolled by galapagos sharks and grey reef sharks. The endemic Easter Island butterflyfish appears in small groups along the upper reef. Visibility is consistently above 40 metres — this is one of the clearest water dives in the world.
getThere: Boat only — 45-minute crossing from Hanga Roa. Exposed to Pacific swells; trips are weather-dependent. Hanga Roa has several dive operators.

name: Hanga Roa Harbour Wrecks
description: The harbour at Hanga Roa holds several deliberately scuttled vessels and an old anchor field from colonial trading ships, resting in 15 to 30 metres on volcanic rubble and sand. Coral encrustation has transformed the hulls into artificial reefs thick with endemic chromis and damselfish. Moray eels of unusual size are habituated to divers, and at night the wrecks come alive with lobsters, crabs, and hunting octopuses. An ideal second dive after the exposed outer sites.
getThere: Boat departure from Hanga Roa dock — 10 minutes. Some wrecks are accessible by shore dive for experienced divers. All licensed dive operators on the island cover this site.

name: Manavai Garden Reef
description: Named after the freshwater garden enclosures the Rapa Nui people carved into the coastline, Manavai is a sheltered reef on the protected western coast that serves as the best macro and coral dive on the island. Dense Pocillopora damicornis coral heads shelter endemic damselfish species and nudibranchs recorded nowhere else. Resident hawksbill turtles feed on sponges at 12 metres. This is the site local dive instructors take new divers — calm conditions and extraordinary biodiversity.
getThere: 15-minute boat ride from Hanga Roa or accessible by shore from the western coast road. Best year-round accessibility of all Easter Island sites.

name: Hio Wall
description: Hio Wall runs along Niue's north coast where the limestone shelf breaks abruptly into open ocean, descending from 10 metres at the reef top to beyond 400. The vertical face is laced with crevices sheltering soldierfish, lionfish, and resting whitetip reef sharks, while the blue water column off the wall draws spinner dolphins and, from June to September, humpback whales so close that divers in the shallows can hear them singing without hydrophones. Visibility here is among the best on the island, often running 50 to 80 metres, and the wall's exposure to the north means it picks up the clearest oceanic water.
getThere: Niue International Airport (IUE) serves Air New Zealand flights from Auckland approximately twice weekly. Hio Wall is on the north coast, a 15 to 20 minute boat ride from Alofi wharf. All boats launch by crane as the island has no sheltered harbour. Book through Niue Dive, the island's primary operator, who monitor north coast swell conditions before committing to this site.

name: Three Islets
description: Three small limestone karst outcrops rising from the sea in the central Mergui Archipelago, each ringed by submerged ledges, caves, and coral gardens between 5 m and 30 m. The shallow walls are encrusted with enormous sea fans and branching wire corals, while nurse sharks pack the caverns under the overhangs. Schools of batfish and trevally rotate around the pinnacles on the current, and seasonal visits from whale sharks make this one of the archipelago's most well-rounded sites for intermediate divers willing to make the liveaboard journey.
getThere: Accessible only by liveaboard from Kawthaung, Myanmar. Three Islets is typically dived on the second or third day of a central Mergui itinerary. Operators include Raja Laut, MV Andaman Tritan, and MV Mermaid. The Myanmar border crossing requires a fee of approximately US$200 to 250 cash paid at Kawthaung port.

name: Western Rocky
description: An exposed granite pinnacle system on the western edge of the Mergui Archipelago, exposed to full Andaman swell and reliably swept by strong currents. This is the site most consistently associated with scalloped hammerhead shark schools in Myanmar: aggregations of 20 to 80 individuals have been documented on the deep northwest face between January and April, rising from 35 m to 20 m on the morning current. Whale sharks are encountered here from March to May, often feeding on plankton concentrated by upwellings around the pinnacle. Grey reef sharks and silvertip sharks maintain a year-round presence. Experienced drift divers only.
getThere: Accessible only by liveaboard from Kawthaung. Western Rocky sits on the exposed western fringe of the archipelago and requires calm sea-state windows — typically December through April only. A DSMB is mandatory; most operators require Advanced Open Water certification and logged drift experience.

name: Shark Cave
description: A shallow limestone cavern system on the southern flank of one of the Mergui karst islands, opening to the reef at 8 m and penetrating roughly 25 m into the rock. The cave interior is a resting ground for whitetip reef sharks — up to 15 individuals have been observed stacked along the sandy cave floor in a single dive — alongside nurse sharks and resting guitar sharks. Outside the cave entrance, a coral garden in 5 to 20 m supports prolific hard and soft coral with high fish diversity. The site requires no cave certification as it is a cavern dive with natural light throughout, but a torch is recommended.
getThere: Accessible by liveaboard from Kawthaung; also possible as a day trip from some Mergui town guesthouses during the dry season. The site's sheltered position inside a bay makes it diveable in conditions that close other sites. A torch is strongly recommended for the cave interior.

name: Sail Rock
description: A single granite pinnacle named for its triangular sail-like profile above water, located in the northern sector of the Mergui Archipelago. Below the surface the rock descends as a near-vertical wall to 38 m on the west side and a stepped reef to 25 m on the east. The wall is dense with sea fans up to 2 m across, barrel sponges, and black coral trees. Silvertip sharks are present year-round at depth; a vertical chimney through the rock at 10 to 18 m is wide enough for single-file passage and is consistently used as a sleeping site by whitetip reef sharks. Whale sharks have been recorded here in March and April on most liveaboard routes.
getThere: Liveaboard only from Kawthaung; Sail Rock falls on the northern Mergui route and is typically dived on itineraries of 7 nights or more. Operators running the northern route include MV Andaman Tritan and MV Mermaid. Currents on the west wall can be sudden and require drift experience.

name: Henry Leith Wreck
description: The Henry Leith is a small coastal freighter that sank in Madang Harbour and now rests upright on a sandy floor at around 18 metres. The wreck is completely encrusted with soft corals and sponges, making it as much a reef as a shipwreck. Lionfish hover in doorways, schools of glassfish fill the holds, and nudibranch hunters will find dozens of species on a single dive. The shallow, calm conditions make this an ideal night dive — torchlight brings out pygmy cuttlefish, bobbit worms and an extraordinary variety of flatworms.
getThere: Depart from Madang town jetty by small boat; 10 to 15 minute ride into the harbour.

name: B-25 Bomber Wreck
description: A WWII-era North American B-25 Mitchell bomber rests in Madang Lagoon, its twin engines, propellers and airframe remarkably intact given the decades of submersion. The aircraft lies on a sandy slope with the cockpit at around 14 metres and the tail at 20 metres, allowing extended bottom time even for recreational divers. Coral growth now covers much of the aluminium structure, and the undercarriage provides shelter for a cleaning station visited by wrasse and small sharks. Aviation history and reef biology combine here in a way that is uniquely Madang.
getThere: Boat departure from Madang town; approximately 20 minutes across the lagoon. Operators mark GPS coordinates.

name: Hon Cau Turtle Bay
description: Hon Cau's sheltered northern bay is Con Dao's most reliable turtle encounter site — a gently sloping reef to 20 meters where green and hawksbill turtles rest on coral bommies and graze on seagrass at the reef base in numbers that reflect decades of national park nesting protection. The site's shallow profile and consistent calm conditions inside the bay make it appropriate for all certification levels, while the outer reef edge adds current-driven pelagic sightings including barracuda schools and trevally. Nesting season from May to September brings nesting females ashore at night on the adjacent beach, making overnight liveaboard stops particularly significant.
getThere: Day trip or liveaboard from Con Son town pier; approximately 35 minutes by speedboat northeast to Hon Cau Island.

name: The Aquarium
description: Named by local dive guides for the density and colour of marine life packed into its sheltered bay, The Aquarium is a shallow coral garden between 3 and 18 meters at the western end of the Con Dao archipelago where biodiversity surveys regularly record over 200 reef fish species in a single dive. The site is defined by exceptionally clear water and negligible current, making it Con Dao's best dedicated macro and underwater photography site — nudibranchs, ghost pipefish, and ornate ghost pipefish are documented year-round, and the rubble zones between coral heads host an unusual density of cephalopods including day-hunting reef octopus. Dugong feeding furrows are visible in the seagrass patches at 8 to 12 meters, indicating regular use even when the animals themselves are not present.
getThere: Day trip from Con Son town pier; approximately 15 minutes by boat west to the sheltered bay at the western end of Con Son Island.

name: Western Rocky
description: Western Rocky is a granite pinnacle system at the southern edge of Myanmar's Mergui Archipelago, positioned where the Andaman Sea deepens sharply and pelagic traffic intensifies — this is the site where liveaboard guides bring divers specifically for open-water shark encounters, including oceanic whitetip and silky sharks that venture onto the plateau during the high season from December through March. The submerged rocks descend to 40 meters on three sides, with the western face exposed to prevailing swell and the heaviest coral growth. Leopard sharks rest on the sandy saddle at 18 meters between the main pinnacle and a smaller satellite rock, and schooling barracuda cloud the blue water above the peak on most morning dives.
getThere: Liveaboard only from Kawthaung; approximately 7 to 9 hours southwest to the far western chain. No day-trip access.

name: North Twin Pinnacle
description: North Twin Island is the northernmost significant dive destination in the Myanmar liveaboard circuit, and its main pinnacle on the island's eastern face is the site most reliably associated with scalloped hammerhead shark aggregations in the Mergui Archipelago — groups of 20 to 60 individuals have been documented at depth between 25 and 40 meters from December through February. The pinnacle rises from 45 meters and is encrusted with pristine table and branching corals on its upper sections, while the deep base transitions to a sand slope where leopard sharks and stingrays rest during the day. The isolation of North Twin means almost no fishing pressure, and the surrounding reef is among the most structurally intact in Myanmar.
getThere: Liveaboard only from Kawthaung; approximately 4 to 5 hours north to North Twin Island in the central-northern Mergui chain. No day-trip access.

name: Night Reef — La Passe de l'Ermitage
description: The reef passage at L'Ermitage undergoes a complete transformation after dark, when the reef fish that shoal visibly during the day retreat into crevices and nocturnal predators take their place — making this one of the best night dives on Réunion and one of the few places in the Indian Ocean where the endemic Réunion bullrout scorpionfish can be reliably found. The bullrout (Scorpaenopsis mauritiana subspecies endemic to the Mascarene Islands) hunts in the shallows from dusk onward, using its cryptic coloration against the reef to ambush reef fish in water as shallow as 4 metres. Octopus emerge to hunt across the sand, cone snails creep along the rubble, and hunting morays probe crevices alongside the torchlit reef.
getThere: L'Ermitage is the northern section of the Saint-Gilles lagoon system, a short drive from Saint-Gilles town centre. Night dives are offered by all Saint-Gilles dive operators with boat departure typically one hour after sunset. Torch rental is available from all operators.

name: La Jaula
description: La Jaula — The Cage — is a submerged coral structure named for the way its tall coral columns and arching spur-and-groove formations create cage-like compartments through which Caribbean reef sharks move with ease. The site is noted for having the highest consistent shark count in Jardines de la Reina, with individual sharks that have been photo-ID catalogued for over 15 years and are demonstrably unfazed by divers. The reef itself is a model of Caribbean reef health: intact branching acroporid corals, dense schools of grunts and snappers over the spurs, and large Nassau grouper holding territory in the grooves. Crocodiles occasionally enter from the nearby mangrove channel and have been observed resting on the sandy floor between coral heads.
getThere: Liveaboard only from Júcaro port; inner archipelago site, accessible on day 2 or 3 of a standard 7-night itinerary.

name: Marsa Alam
description: Marsa Alam (Arabic: مَرْسَىٰ عَلَم Marsā ʿAlam [ˈmæɾsæ ˈʕælæm], Classical Arabic lit. 'Anchorage Mountain') is a tourist town in south-eastern Egypt, located on the western shore of the Red Sea.

name: MS Logna
description: MV Logna was built as general cargo ship in Bergens Mekaniske Verksted,  Shipyard,  Norway  in 1958. She transported cargo between Norway   and Spain  until 1969, when she was acquired by the Bahama Cement Company.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Tiger Beach, Bahamas. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.
notes: Added via free-API enrichment. Source count: 1.

name: Chinhoyi Caves
description: The Chinhoyi Caves (previously the Sinoia Caves) are a group of limestone and dolomite caves in north central Zimbabwe. Designated a National Park in 1955, and managed by the Zimbabwe Parks & Wildlife Management Authority.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Chinhoyi Caves, Zimbabwe. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.
notes: Added via free-API enrichment. Source count: 1.

name: Hoi Ha Wan
description: Hoi Ha Wan (Chinese: 海下灣) or Jone's Cove is a bay at the north of Sai Kung Peninsula. It is part of Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park, a marine park in Hong Kong.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Hoi Ha Wan, Hong Kong. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.

name: Hranice Abyss
description: Hranice Abyss (Czech: Hranická propast) is the deepest flooded pit cave in the world. It is a karst sinkhole near the town of Hranice, Czech Republic.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Hranice Abyss, Czech Republic. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.
notes: Added via free-API enrichment. Source count: 1.

name: Columbus Passage
description: Columbus Passage is a coral dive site near Providenciales, Turks and Caicos. Mentioned across 1 authoritative dive guides, it is considered one of the region's most notable dive destinations.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Providenciales, Turks and Caicos. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.

name: Escambron Marine Park
description: Escambron Marine Park is a coral dive site near San Juan, Puerto Rico. Mentioned across 1 authoritative dive guides, it is considered one of the region's most notable dive destinations.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving San Juan, Puerto Rico. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.
notes: Added via free-API enrichment. Source count: 1.

name: Socotra
description: Socotra, locally known as Saqatri, is a Yemeni island in the Indian Ocean. It is situated between the Gulf of Aden, the Guardafui Channel and the Arabian Sea, and lies near major shipping routes.
getThere: Fly into the nearest international airport serving Socotra, Yemen. Local transfer options vary — check with your dive operator for current logistics.
notes: Added via free-API enrichment. Source count: 1.

name: Coral Garden
description: Sloping coral garden in Sogod Bay featuring pristine hard and soft corals, steep drop-offs to walls, and healthy reef ecosystem. Entry on shallow slope with scattered coral heads and sand transitions to deeper walls. Excellent for macro and wide-angle photography with reliable visibility.
getThere: Fly into Tacloban Airport (Philippines). 3.5-hour van transfer to Padre Burgos, Sogod Bay. Alternatively, fly into Cebu and ferry to Leyte, then 2-hour van transfer. Dive site accessible by boat from Padre Burgos area resorts within 10-30 minutes.
notes: Marine Protected Area (MPA); part of Sogod Bay conservation network. Diveable year-round. June-August offers best weather and visibility. November-May whale shark season (though sightings not guaranteed). Protected coral area—follow local guidelines. Mild to moderate currents depending on season.

name: Derawan House Reef
description: Shallow reef accessible from Derawan Island's beach and jetty with abundant green sea turtles, nudibranchs, and macro critters. Fringing reef gently sloping into deeper coral gardens, ideal for night dives and check-out dives. Clear macro habitat with typical depths 5–15m on the reef plateau.
getThere: Fly to Balikpapan (BPN), then 45-minute connection to Berau (BEJ). Road transfer 1.5–2 hours to Tanjung Batu port. 30-minute speedboat to Derawan Island (IDR 50,000–100,000/person). Accessible year-round; January stormy conditions may affect resorts.
notes: Green turtles present at jetty nightly; site used for check-out dives and night diving. No stinging jellyfish. Part of Berau marine protected area. Reef has recovered from past dynamite/cyanide fishing damage; now healthy with soft and hard coral growth. Entry via beach or jetty; no boat required for access.

name: Sail Rock
description: Isolated granite pinnacle rising 15m above the surface and 40m below, featuring a dramatic vertical chimney swim-through. Renowned for massive schools of chevron barracuda, abundant pelagic fish, and frequent whale shark encounters. Strong currents and thermoclines common below 25m.
getThere: Accessible via day trips from Koh Samui (50 min by speedboat from Bangrak Pier), Koh Phangan (1 hour), or Koh Tao (1.5–2 hours). International flights via Surat Thani Airport (~2 hours to Koh Samui) or Bangkok (~7 hours). Book through established dive operators in advance.
notes: Open offshore site; strong currents and thermoclines below 25m. Mandatory nitrox training beneficial. Designated for advanced divers; Open Water diver minimum but Advanced Open Water strongly recommended. Check moon phases and weather—trips often cancelled during full moon or monsoon conditions (October–November particularly challenging). Permits unnecessary but dive operators registered with Thai authorities.

name: Southwest Pinnacle
description: Multi-peaked granite pinnacle rising from 30m sand to 5m, draped in anemones and black coral. Granite formations in circular pattern attract schools of fusiliers, snappers, and barracuda. Notable for giant groupers, stingrays in overhangs, and seasonal whale shark encounters. Strong currents common; visibility typically 15–30m.
getThere: Fly to Koh Samui (15 min flight from Bangkok). Ferry or speedboat 1.5 hours to Koh Tao. Southwest Pinnacle: 45-minute boat ride southwest from Koh Tao's main pier (Big Blue Diving, Isla Tortuga, Discovery Divers operate regular trips).
notes: Open ocean site 4 nm offshore; strong currents possible. Advanced Open Water certification minimum; deep specialty recommended. Best morning dives (early pelagic activity). Seasonal whale shark encounters March–May, August–September. Multiple dive operators on Koh Tao offer daily trips year-round. No specific permits required. Site occasionally inaccessible during monsoon swells (November–January) but remains diveable.

name: Roma
description: Submerged seamount rising from 200m to 8m off northern Tomia Island, crowned with distinctive potato coral formations resembling Rome's Coliseum. Healthy coral garden with abundant schooling fish and macro life.
getThere: Fly to Makassar (Sultan Hasanuddin International), connect via Wings Air/Lion Air to Matahora Airport in Wakatobi (~1h50m), then speedboat to Tomia Island. Wakatobi Resort also runs direct charter flights from Bali (~2.5h).
notes: Flagship coral garden dive of Wakatobi. Seamount topography lets divers work coral coverage from ~25m up to 8m with little current. Diveable year-round. Small coral formations resemble Rome's Coliseum, hence the name.

name: Koh Rong Corner
description: Shallow coral reef site featuring a rocky corner formation with steep cliff face. Young reef with coral-covered rocks, sandy areas, and abundant small shark species including bamboo and coral catsharks, nudibranchs, barrel sponges, and colorful reef fish. Light to moderate currents support drift diving.
getThere: Fly to Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville International Airport, then ferry from Sihanoukville mainland to Koh Rong Island (45 min to 2 hours). Dive centers based in Koh Touch Village.
notes: Koh Rong Corner is the PADI-indexed most notable dive site on Koh Rong. Light to moderate currents make this a suitable drift dive. Best visibility March through April; southwest monsoon (May-October) reduces visibility and increases current.

name: Tokai Maru & SMS Cormoran Twin Wrecks
description: The world's only site where a WWI and WWII wreck touch: SMS Cormoran (German merchant raider, scuttled 1917) and Tokai Maru (Japanese freighter, sunk 1943). Both rest on the harbor floor at around 37m. Advanced wreck dive with penetration access to engine rooms and cargo holds, the upper structure reachable near 12m.
getThere: Apra Harbor is on Guam's west coast near Piti village. Fly into Guam International Airport (GUM), about 10 km south, then rental car or taxi (~30 min). Sites reached by dive boat; wreck penetration requires a Wreck Diver certification.
notes: Unique historical significance: the only place on Earth where a WWI and a WWII wreck make contact. Inner-harbor turbidity keeps visibility around 10m; dive lines essential due to depth, penetration, and shipping traffic.

name: Itsandra Reef
description: Coral plateau and volcanic cave system off Itsandra Beach featuring depths from shallow reefs to deep lava formations. Active volcano topography creates a dramatic underwater landscape with grey reef sharks, sea turtles, and seasonal humpback whale encounters.
getThere: Fly to Moroni International Airport (HAH) on Grande Comore, then taxi or arranged transfer about 30km south to Itsandra Beach (20 to 30 minutes). Local dive operator at Itsandra Beach Hotel provides boat access.
notes: Site sits off Itsandra Beach on Grande Comore, roughly 15km south of Mitsamiouli town. Volcanic topography with lava tubes and caves. Coelacanths inhabit deep caves well beyond recreational limits. Some monthly condition figures are interpolated from regional data. Best conditions June through September; November through April is cyclone season.

name: Bone de Jockey
description: Enormous isolated rock pinnacle with prolific marine life and multiple dive sites around its boulder formation. Endemic species, massive groupers, moray eels, octopuses, and rays inhabit rock crevices and sandy seabed.
getThere: By boat from Atlantic Diving Center in Santana, Sao Tome. Approximately 15 to 30 minutes boat ride from the dive center.
notes: Enormous rock formation with several distinct dive areas. Thermocline present at 15 to 20m depth. Diving limited to 30m maximum on the island due to no decompression facility.

name: Back Door
description: Boulder-strewn macro dive featuring massive underwater rock formations that create ideal ecosystems for small reef fish. Excellent for macro photography with nudibranchs, batfish, and barracuda sheltering among the boulders. Exclusive to Koh Rong-based divers.
getThere: 20 minute boat ride from Koh Rong Dive Center at Koh Touch Village; 2 hour ferry from Sihanoukville then local operator transfer
notes: Macro dive exclusive to Koh Rong-based divers. Best during dry season November to April. Boulder formations shelter small critters. Restricted visibility May to October during southwest monsoon.

name: Earl of Shaftesbury
description: Iron four-mast sailing ship wrecked in 1893 off Akurala, now a thriving artificial reef at 14 meters. Covered in corals and marine life including sweetlips, stingrays, barracuda, and batfish. The wreck rests on sandy bottom with bow and stern sections relatively intact, bow masts still recognizable.
getThere: About 15 minutes by boat from Hikkaduwa town center; local dive operators run regular trips with hotel pickup.
notes: Iron sailing ship wrecked May 1893 after striking a reef. Protected archaeological site. Bow and stern recognizable with iron masts still standing. Best November to April; June to September monsoon.

name: Beomseom (Tiger Island)
description: Uninhabited volcanic island named for its resemblance to a crouching tiger, featuring dramatic basalt formations, sea caves with cathedral arches, and vibrant soft coral gardens. Rich with diverse temperate and subtropical marine life across depths ranging 7-27m. UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
getThere: Boat from Seogwipo Port, about 5km southwest, roughly 15 minutes. PADI operators in Seogwipo run trips.
notes: Named for its resemblance to a crouching tiger. Sea caves with cathedral-arch formations. Natural monument and UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with restricted access; arrange permits with operators. Peak diving September to November.

name: West Island
description: Turtle-shaped West Island lies in Sanya Bay's National Coral Reef Reserve, featuring 41 documented reef fish species and vibrant staghorn and crown coral. Clear waters host colorful tropical fish including clownfish, groupers, and trevally across sandy and rocky substrates with abundant sea urchins and anemones.
getThere: From Sanya city center about 25 to 30 minutes by car to Xidao Wharf, then a 10 to 15 minute boat ride to West Island in the National Coral Reef Reserve.
notes: Second largest island in Hainan, part of China's largest National Coral Reef Reserve. 41 reef fish species documented via environmental DNA. Calm bay waters suit Open Water divers. Typical max dive depth around 12m.

name: Electric Nose
description: A dramatic pinnacle dive rising from 50 meters toward the surface, featuring steep walls draped in soft corals and macro life. The site is known for hosting over 50 nudibranch species and encounters with schooling snappers, trevally, and barracuda. Steep drop-offs and rock formations make it one of Nha Trang's most photogenic dives.
getThere: Boat access only from Nha Trang town, about 1 to 2 hours depending on conditions. Booked through established operators. Located on the easterly end of Hon Noc island.
notes: Also known as Rer Rond. Established as a dive site by Rainbow Divers in 1997. Pinnacle rises from about 50 meters. Macro hotspot with over 50 nudibranch species. Requires Advanced Open Water due to depth and current. Best on slack tides.

name: Aride Bank
description: Dramatic granite seamount rising from deep water off the northernmost granitic island in Seychelles. Strong southeast trade wind currents concentrate large pelagic fish, reef sharks, groupers, and rays around the boulder structure, with soft coral gardens and swaying sea fans in the shallows.
getThere: Fly to Mahe (SEZ), connect to Praslin by air or ferry, then a 30 to 45 minute dive boat ride north past Curieuse and Aride Island. Site is reliably accessible only in the calmer northwest monsoon months.
notes: Exposed site with strong currents when running; a reef hook is useful. Boat access is often difficult during the southeast monsoon (June to September).

name: Dale Point
description: Rocky point near the mouth of Milford Sound known for friendly octopus encounters and forests of black coral. A permanent tannin stained freshwater layer sits over the salt water, cutting the light so that deep water black coral, Antipathella fiordensis, grows in only 15 to 20 metres. The result is a dark twilight dive with life normally found far deeper.
getThere: Fly to Queenstown (ZQN), then drive about four hours over the Crown Range to Milford Sound, or take a scenic flight. Dive boats reach Dale Point from Milford Marina in 30 to 45 minutes.
notes: Advanced and drysuit experience expected. The freshwater layer gives a sharp halocline and low surface visibility that opens up below the tannin layer. Rainfall makes the dark layer thicker.

name: Hospital Point
description: Fringing reef off the northwest tip of Isla Solarte, named for an old United Fruit Company hospital ashore. Shallow lettuce and brain coral gardens roll over into a wall that drops to about 15 metres, with parrotfish, wrasse, and seahorses by day and nurse sharks and lobster active at night. Calm and close to Bocas Town.
getThere: Fly to Bocas Town (BOC) on Isla Colon, then a 5 to 10 minute water taxi to the northwest tip of Isla Solarte. Reef entry is from an anchored boat into the shallows.
notes: Accessible reef popular for training, snorkelling, and night dives. Visibility drops in the rainy season; best in the September to October window and February to March.

name: Torre Guaceto Reef
description: A representative dive across the heart of the Torre Guaceto reserve, from shallow Posidonia seagrass meadows and rocky ledges near the old watchtower down to a coralligenous platform around 20 to 40 metres. This is one of the Mediterranean's clearest recovery stories, where fully protecting a small core brought back seabream, octopus, moray and lobster in numbers you rarely see on the open coast. Access is managed by the reserve, so diving here runs through authorised guides rather than open recreational entry.
getThere: Fly into Brindisi (BDS), around 25 km south. The reserve sits on the Adriatic coast between Carovigno and Brindisi, with summer access to Punta Penna Grossa by shuttle or bike. Diving inside the protected area is arranged through the reserve and authorised operators, so book ahead rather than turning up to dive.
notes: Diving inside the Torre Guaceto reserve is restricted and managed. General recreational diving is limited, and access runs through the reserve and authorised guides rather than open entry. Zone A is a fully protected no entry core reserved for science and enforcement.

name: Santo Antao Wreck
description: A 55-meter merchant vessel that sank in 1966, now a shallow artificial reef broken into three sections. It serves as a nursery for hundreds of pufferfish and draws nurse sharks and moray eels into its hull. Limited penetration is possible for certified wreck divers.
getThere: Located about 10 minutes by boat from Santa Maria harbor on Sal Island. Dive operators in Santa Maria offer hotel transfers to the dive center.
notes: Sharp edges on the wreck; watch equipment. Penetration limited to two small entry points and requires wreck certification. Nursery for pufferfish; humpback whales pass during the March-May migration.

name: HMS Cricket
description: A British river gunboat built in 1915 and later scuttled off Larnaca Bay, now resting inverted between about 29 and 32 meters. A sandy depression beneath the hull lets divers circle the wreck, while open hatches and tight interior passages reward careful wreck technique. A quieter deep alternative to the nearby Zenobia.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: 7mm wetsuit or drysuit for deep dives

getThere: Fly into Larnaca International Airport (LCA), then a short drive to Larnaca harbour. The wreck sits offshore in Larnaca Bay and is reached by dive boat, roughly a 15 to 20 minute transit.
notes: A deep, advanced wreck. Penetration is for suitably trained divers only, and decompression obligations are common after a full exploration. Watch depth and silt inside the hull.

name: Napantao Marine Sanctuary
description: One of the oldest protected reefs in Sogod Bay, where a steep wall drops away carpeted in giant gorgonian fans and soft corals. Currents along the wall pull in trevally and barracuda, seasonal whale sharks cruise the bay, and the coral bommies hide rich macro life. Visibility often exceeds 30 meters in good conditions.

Spring suit to 3mm; tail end of whale shark season

getThere: Fly into Tacloban (TAC) from Manila or Cebu, then transfer about 2 to 3 hours south to the Padre Burgos dive resorts on Sogod Bay. The sanctuary itself lies across the bay off San Francisco municipality and is reached by a short boat ride.
notes: A community managed marine sanctuary; a small fee usually applies and supports local protection. The wall is deep and currents can be strong, so it suits experienced divers. Whale shark encounters are seasonal and never guaranteed.

name: Dabaisha
description: A boat dive off Green Island's southern coast where a white sand bottom rises into soft coral pinnacles and small caverns. Schools of copper sweepers fill the overhangs and collapsed cave ceilings let shafts of light through, while green turtles are seen through much of the warmer season. One of the flagship sites for diving in Taiwan.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: 2mm wetsuit or rash guard; typhoon risk late month
2mm wetsuit or rash guard; typhoon season
3 to 5mm wetsuit; northeast winds pick up

getThere: Reach Green Island by ferry from Taitung on Taiwan's southeast coast, a 50 to 60 minute crossing, or by short domestic flight. Taitung connects to Taipei and Kaohsiung. Ferries depend on sea conditions, so build in buffer time.
notes: The pinnacles, caverns and light chimney reward good buoyancy control, and currents can sweep the point, so plan around slack windows. Mostly a boat dive. Peak season is roughly May to October.

name: Cupcakes
description: Twin volcanic rocks break the surface here, and divers work the channels and sand shelves between them past small caves and swim throughs. Schools of king angelfish sweep the rock while white tip reef sharks rest on the sand. In the cool water season the site is a reliable spot for giant Pacific manta rays feeding in the current.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: Shorty or rash guard; green season

getThere: Fly into Liberia (LIR) in Guanacaste, then transfer to Playa Flamingo or Tamarindo. Dive boats reach the Catalina Islands in roughly 40 minutes from the beach.
notes: Manta season runs through the cooler, current heavy months around December to April, when cold upwelling drops visibility and water temperature. Currents can be strong.

name: The Zoo
description: A gently sloping macro site where coral bommies rise from fine sand and shelter one of Wakatobi's densest concentrations of critters. Frogfish, ghost pipefish, pygmy seahorses and leaf fish reward a slow, close search, and at dusk mandarin fish emerge to mate among the rubble. A rewarding night dive for photographers and macro hunters.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: 3mm wetsuit; calm seas, peak season begins

getThere: Fly to Wangi-Wangi (WNI) in the Wakatobi Regency via Makassar on Sulawesi, connecting from Jakarta or Bali. Resorts and liveaboards arrange boat transfers to the dive sites.
notes: A sheltered site that suits skill building as well as serious macro photography. Dusk dives target the mandarin fish mating window. Move slowly and keep hands off the reef to spot cryptic critters.

name: Rašip
description: A rocky Adriatic wall that drops steeply into clear blue water off the islet of Rašip in Kornati National Park. Morays and conger eels fill the crevices, dentex and amberjack patrol the deeper blue, and spiny lobsters shelter under ledges. Visibility is often excellent, showing off the bare, sculpted limestone that defines the Kornati.
getThere: Fly into Split (SPU), then drive about 1.5 hours to Murter on the Dalmatian coast. Licensed operators run boats into Kornati National Park, with Rašip roughly 8 nautical miles offshore.
notes: Diving inside Kornati National Park requires a permit and a licensed operator. The wall is deep and best suited to experienced divers; plan depth and gas carefully.

name: Ilha do Farol
description: Rocky reef near the 7 meter lighthouse on Alcatrazes main island. Clear water, healthy corals and good reef fish habitat. Green turtles, hawksbill turtles and scalloped hammerhead sharks frequent the area. Moderate currents and seasonal clarity swings. Boat access only through ICMBio authorized operators.
getThere: Fly to São Paulo (GRU or CGH). Drive 2 hours to São Sebastião. Depart from Ilhabela or São Sebastião with ICMBio authorized operators. Boat ride approximately 2 to 3 hours offshore.
notes: Protected marine refuge. Diving only with ICMBio authorized guides and operators. Weather sensitive site best visited calm conditions November to May. Rocky bottom with no sheltered entry.

name: Punta Cahuita
description: The tip of Cahuita National Park protects Costa Rica's largest coral reef. The reef begins in shallow 1 to 2 meter waters extending to 5 to 10 meters at interesting coral formations. Brain corals the size of washing machines, sea fans, gorgonians, and staghorn corals dominate. Over 500 fish species including parrotfish, angelfish, damselfish, and green moray eels inhabit the reef. Green sea turtles, nurse sharks, and stingrays are common sightings.
getThere: Cahuita is accessible via the Caribbean Coastal Highway from San Jose (approximately 3.5 hours) or Puerto Viejo (30 minutes north). Access the reef via guided snorkel tour boats departing from Cahuita village or Puerto Vargas station. All reef entry requires a licensed guide and park entry fee.
notes: Snorkeling requires a guided tour, available daily from $35 to 55 USD per person. Park entry approximately $5 to 10 USD. Green moray eels are predictable residents in reef crevices but do not bite unless provoked. June and July visibility is severely reduced by silt from the Estrella River during heavy rains. Morning dives yield best visibility and light. Snorkeling is restricted to depths of 2 to 10 meters; scuba diving to a maximum of 40 feet (12 meters) for recreational diving.

name: Peyrefite Snorkel Trail
description: Protected 250 meter marked snorkel trail with 5 observation stations representing different Mediterranean habitats: pebble beds, Posidonia seagrass meadows, rocky blocks, fault lines, and deep drops. Equipment rental available on the beach. Open June through September only.
getThere: Nearest airport is Perpignan, 45 km north. From Banyuls sur Mer town center, head toward Peyrefite beach where the marked trail begins. Masks, fins and audio guides are available for rent on site.
notes: Open June through September only. Trail features 5 observation stations marked by buoys. Suitable for families and beginners. No certification required for snorkeling.

name: Western Reefs
description: Rocky reefs west of the main beach in shallow to moderate depths. Large crayfish and snapper inhabit these reefs alongside occasional giant boarfish and stingrays in summer months. Accessible from Goat Island Beach.
getThere: From Auckland, drive approximately 80 minutes north to Leigh on Auckland's north shore. Goat Island Beach is accessed via a short walk from the main carpark. Entry via shore dive from the beach.
notes: Marine reserve, no take zone. No spearfishing or collection of marine life permitted. Protected area requires respect for wildlife. Southerly winds provide calmest conditions.

name: Kisite Island
description: Coral reef dive site off Kisite Island in the marine national park. The reef hosts green sea turtles, spinner dolphins, and reef fish including grouper, wrasse, and pufferfish. Clear water and gentle slopes make this accessible for beginners seeking coral and large marine animals.
getThere: Fly into Mombasa International Airport (MBA), 70km north. Drive south to Shimoni village on the Kwale coast, about 2.5 hours from Mombasa. Access the site by traditional dhow or motorboat from Shimoni Pier, a 20 to 30 minute crossing to Kisite Island. Contact Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) warden at Shimoni Pier for permits and boat arrangements.
notes: Marine national park entry permit required, managed by Kenya Wildlife Service. Site sits within a no take protected area. Check with local operators for current conditions and seasonal marine animal sightings before diving.

name: Tanikely Sud
description: A drift dive at a shallow drop off featuring magnificent coral architecture with large coral spurs. The reef top offers superb hard and soft corals between 2 and 6 meters, while sand patches extend to 20 meters. The small drop off reveals gorgonian sea fans and diverse marine fauna including leopard sharks, snappers, barracudas, bonito, and large lobsters. Sea turtles are regularly encountered among the coral gardens. This site is part of the protected Nosy Tanikely marine reserve.
getThere: Located 12 kilometers from Nosy Be off northwest Madagascar, Tanikely Sud is typically reached by 30 to 40 minute speedboat journey from Nosy Be town or nearby dive resorts. Day trips depart daily from Nosy Be with local dive operators or snorkel tour providers.
notes: Nosy Tanikely is a protected marine reserve and national park (no take zone). Day visitors only; no overnight accommodations on the island. Snorkeling and diving available year round. The site is especially known for reliable sea turtle encounters and excellent coral formations suitable for all certification levels.

name: Siete Pecados Reef
description: Seven limestone islets with healthy coral reefs and abundant marine life in calm shallow water. The site is renowned for schools of great barracudas congregating around the easternmost peak in clear water. Groupers, sweetlips, batfish and reef fish thrive across the coral formations. The strict no fishing and no anchoring policy has preserved the ecosystem.
getThere: Fly to Busuanga Airport (Coron) from Manila or Cebu. Travel to Coron town by land transfer. Boats depart daily from Coron town pier for the 30 minute journey to Siete Pecados Marine Park.
notes: Marine park entrance fee required. Strict no fishing and no anchoring policy. Site is a marine sanctuary. Water can be murky June to September due to monsoon rains.

name: Twin Peaks
description: Two prominent coral covered pinnacles rising from the seabed near Siete Pecados. The site features extensive hard and soft coral formations and abundant macro life including nudibranchs, frogfish and moray eels. Green sea turtles are commonly observed grazing on algae. Eagle rays patrol the deeper sections. The coral gardens attract photographers and macro enthusiasts.
getThere: Fly to Busuanga Airport (Coron) from Manila or Cebu. Travel to Coron town by land transfer. Boats depart daily from Coron town pier for approximately 40 minute journey to Twin Peaks.
notes: Twin Peaks is located near Siete Pecados Marine Park. The site is often included in multi site snorkeling and diving tours from Coron. Moderate current possible during peak season.

name: Cleft Island
description: Granite island dive site featuring massive 8 metre high granite boulders on a 20 metre deep reef. Huge swim throughs, overhangs and sea caves at shallow depths transition to spectacular deep sponge gardens at 20 to 30 metres depth. Colourful gardens of giant sponges, jewel anemones, ascidians and yellow zoanthids cover underwater caves and ledges. Also known as Skull Rock due to its distinctive cranium shape when viewed from certain angles.
getThere: Access by boat only. Depart from Tidal River visitor area (approximately 3 hours drive from Melbourne) or arrange a charter with local dive operators based in the Promontory region. Cleft Island is located approximately 2.5 kilometres south east of the mainland tip of Wilson's Promontory. Typical boat transit time from shore is 30 to 45 minutes depending on sea conditions.
notes: Site is within Wilson's Promontory Marine National Park, a no take marine reserve. Strict no fishing regulations apply. Diving possible November to May during best conditions. Winter diving (June to August) is possible but requires drysuit and experience with strong currents and reduced visibility. Guide or local knowledge recommended due to exposed location and potentially strong conditions.

name: Norman Bay South
description: Boulder field and granite reef dive site located at the southern end of Norman Bay on the western side of Wilson's Promontory. Boulders slope down to sandy bottom at approximately 18 metres depth. Large granite formations create small swim throughs and overhangs in shallow water. Accessible by boat and used by recreational diving operators as a reliable site with varied depths suitable for divers building experience.
getThere: Access by boat. Located near Tidal River visitor area on the western side of Wilson's Promontory. Norman Bay is accessible from the Tidal River parking area (approximately 3 hours drive from Melbourne). Charter dive boats and snorkeling operations depart from nearby operators. Boat transit time from shore is typically 15 to 25 minutes.
notes: Within Wilson's Promontory Marine National Park no take marine reserve. Suitable for recreational divers with open water certification. The site offers varied depths from 5 to 18 metres allowing divers to stay within comfortable depth range. Best diving November to May when water temperature reaches 15 to 20 degrees Celsius and visibility improves.

name: Barracuda Point, Kakaban
description: Steep outer-reef wall on Kakaban's southeast tip delivering schooling barracuda, sharks, and tuna in fierce current. A grab line secures divers at 24m on the upcurrent face before pelagic action unfolds.
