getThere: Fly to Balikpapan (BPP), Indonesia. Transfer 3.5 hours by car to Tanjung Redeb, then boat 45min to Kakaban Island. Most divers book liveaboards or lodge-based operators from Sangalaki/Maratua nearby.
notes: Advanced certification required due to strong current (>2 knots) and depth. A grab line is permanently installed at 24m on the upcurrent side. Maximum bottom time 30-35 minutes. Site often inaccessible January; confirm access before booking. Drift diving standard.

name: Chomoni
description: East coast wall dive featuring dramatic volcanic topography and gorgonian coral gardens. Accessible from the village beach; descends from 15m through sheltered shallow plateau into steep drop-offs reaching 55m. Strong whale song presence during migration season.
getThere: Moroni international airport (HAH) via Air Austral or Precision Air. 1.5 hour drive to Chomoni village on eastern coast. Local boat access from village beach to dive site.
notes: Only established dive site on Grande Comore's east coast. Well sheltered December-March. Humpback whale migration July-October creates unique acoustic diving experience. Approach via zodiac from village. Site accessible for open-water certified divers on calmer days.

name: Sharp Island
description: Known as the Maldives of Hong Kong, Sharp Island features exceptional coral gardens with 77.5% hard coral coverage. Shallow depths and calm conditions make it ideal for beginners. Diverse reef fish community with moray eels, cuttlefish, and wrasses among 300+ recorded species. Famous for large Pavona coral fields and brain coral formations.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: 5mm full wetsuit with hood and vest
5mm full wetsuit with hood and vest

getThere: From Hong Kong International Airport (60km west), travel to Sai Kung Town. Boat access via Pak Sha Wan pier or other local piers. Sharp Island is within Kiu Tsui Country Park, approximately 12km northeast of Hoi Ha Wan. Most dive operators run April-December.
notes: Sharp Island is part of Kiu Tsui Country Park and has designated coral anchors managed by AFCD. Diving concentrated on western shores. Best diving on days with easterly/northeasterly winds. Marine protected area with high conservation value (third highest coral coverage among 36 Hong Kong survey sites). Particularly popular in summer monsoon season due to shelter from waves.

name: Koh Yippon Lek
description: Small rocky island at northern Ang Thong with a submerged 20-meter cave system featuring air pockets and archways. Colorful soft coral gardens, anemone beds, and abundant reef fish. Requires good buoyancy control. Seasonal whale shark encounters.
getThere: Nearest airport: Koh Samui International (USM), 25km south. Ferry from Koh Samui to Ang Thong Marine Park pier, then speedboat 30 minutes to Koh Yippon Lek.
notes: Park open February-October. Cave diving requires good buoyancy control and moderate experience. Accessible mainly via day trips from Koh Samui.

name: Salpatxot
description: Small reef on northern face of La Meda Gran with scattered large rock blocks on Posidonia seagrass meadow. Rock formation (Salpatxot) marks reference point. Teeming with groupers, moray eels, and octopuses; sandy areas harbor rare pen shells. Moonfish sightings possible in June.
getThere: Fly to Barcelona (189 km southwest). Drive northeast 2.5 hours to L'Estartit. Boat access only via licensed diving operators in L'Estartit; site accessed in ~15 minutes from coast.
notes: Protected marine reserve; only licensed operators permitted. No spearfishing or collection allowed. Posidonia seagrass meadows fragile; avoid stirring sediment. Pinna nobilis critically endangered—observe only. Moderate currents can occur; stay near reference rock.

name: Samran Pinnacle
description: Deep granite pinnacle in open water between Sail Rock and Koh Tao. Drops from 9m to 28m with strong currents and prolific pelagic action. Schools of yellowback fusiliers, chevron barracuda, and jacks create spectacular underwater encounters.
getThere: Fly to Bangkok or Phuket, transfer to Koh Tao (2-3 hours from Bangkok). Dive operators in Koh Tao run 45-90 minute boat trips to Samran Pinnacle.
notes: Advanced divers only due to strong open-ocean currents. Site exposed to the water channel between Koh Tao and Koh Phangan; access limited during November-December monsoon. Whale shark sightings most reliable March-May and September-October.

name: Davíðsgjá
description: Freshwater tectonic fissure in Thingvallavatn Lake featuring crystal-clear glacial waters filtered through lava formations. Home to endemic dwarf Arctic char and other cold-water species. Often described as Silfra's darker, spookier sibling with more dramatic rock formations.
getThere: Located in Þingvellir National Park, 40 km northeast of Reykjavik via Route 36. Approximately 45 km from Keflavik International Airport, 1 hour drive. Access via park entrance; diving organized through local operators.
notes: Seasonal availability April-October; occasionally accessible November-March with good weather. Year-round dry suit required (water 2-4°C). Freshwater fissure with visibility more weather-dependent than Silfra. Advanced booking recommended. Site capacity limited.

name: Barracuda Reef
description: A vibrant coral-encrusted mini-wall starting at 15 meters with dramatic vertical drop-offs and overhangs. This lava flow reef is famous for massive schools of barracuda patrolling the walls and ledges packed with queen angelfish, nurse sharks resting in shadows, lobsters, and moray eels. Excellent for spotting reef sharks and diverse reef tropicals.
getThere: Fly into St. Eustatius airport (Airports code: TJSJ, usually via connecting flights through San Juan, Puerto Rico, or St. Maarten). Ground transfers to dive shops in Oranjestad take 15-20 minutes. Barracuda Reef is accessed by boat dive from Golden Rock Dive Center or Statia Divers, approximately 10-15 minutes from shore.
notes: Site is moored to protect the reef. No anchoring allowed. Sint Eustatius Marine Park requires all divers respect protected areas and marine wildlife. Drift diving possible when currents stronger; operators conduct pre-dive current checks.

name: Half Moon Caye Wall
description: Dramatic vertical coral wall descending from shallow reef crest at 9m to abyssal depths beyond 40m. Caribbean reef sharks cruise the walls year-round; manta rays congregate in March. Schools of groupers, snappers, and angelfish on coral-encrusted surfaces. Minimal current, exceptional visibility in dry season.
getThere: 55 miles east of Belize City. Fly to Belize City International Airport (BZE), transfer by boat from San Pedro, Ambergris Caye (40 minutes) or Caye Caulker (1 hour) to Lighthouse Reef Atoll. Live-aboard operations also available.
notes: Part of Lighthouse Reef Marine Protected Area. No spearfishing. Advanced wall diving technique recommended. Spawning aggregation of Nassau grouper occurs December-January.

name: Davíðsgjá Fissure
description: A dramatic, lesser-known fissure hidden within Lake Thingvallavatn, Davíðsgjá diverges between tectonic plates with branching narrow passages and towering gorge walls. Crystal-clear glacial waters reveal 100+ meters of visibility in an intimate geological cathedral.
getThere: 45 km northeast of Reykjavik via Route 1 and Route 36 into Thingvellir National Park. International flights to Keflavik (KEF), 50 minutes transfer. Located on Lake Thingvallavatn's north shore.
notes: Requires PADI Open Water minimum plus 10 logged dry suit dives. Physically demanding entry over lava terrain with full equipment. Weather-dependent in winter (Nov-Mar). Often combined with Silfra for comprehensive rift diving experience.

name: Cap l'Abeille
description: Rocky cape dive site featuring extensive coral formations and abundant fish life. Strong presence of dusky grouper and dentex among rocky reefs at 16-30m. Part of France's first marine nature reserve with 1,200+ species. Upper sections at 5-12m ideal for decompression and macro observation.
getThere: Nearest airport Barcelona (190km, 2.5 hours) or Perpignan (50km, 45 minutes). Transfer to Banyuls-sur-Mer on Mediterranean coast. Cap l'Abeille accessed via beach entry at Plage de Taillelauque near Les Espérades, on RD 114 road between Banyuls and Cerbère.
notes: Part of Cerbère-Banyuls Marine Nature Reserve (France's first protected marine area, 1974). Protected access—no spearfishing. Avoid east and south winds. Multiple buoys allow several dive routes. Upper sections optimal for decompression and observations.

name: Floors Reef
description: Pinnacle reef featuring a 14m-high rocky rise from 24m sand bottom, positioned in Cape Rodney's strong tidal flow. Dense sponge gardens and filterfeeders attract abundant pelagics and schooling fish. Advanced current dive with exceptional biodiversity.

conditionsByMonth.suitRecommendation: 7mm full body with hood and booties

getThere: Auckland International Airport (AKL), approximately 100km (1.5 hours) south of Leigh. Rent vehicle or arrange shuttle to Leigh village. Boat access from Goat Island Dive (licensed operator) required; moorings on-site.
notes: Strong current year-round—experienced divers and boat operator mandatory. Diver must locate anchor warp underwater for exit due to current strength. Best conditions: southerly winds (flat sea) and calm swell. Avoid northerly winds which increase turbidity. Marine reserve regulations apply; check with operators for current restrictions.

name: Piti Bomb Holes Marine Preserve
description: A protected marine preserve featuring natural percolation pits that resemble bomb craters in the reef flat. Home to over 200 fish species and 100 coral varieties, offering accessible snorkeling and diving with green sea turtles, barracuda, and dense anemone beds in crystal-clear water.
getThere: Fly into Guam International Airport (GUM), about 15 km south of Piti. Piti Bomb Holes is reached by boat from local dive operators in Tumon Bay, about 20-30 minutes transit. Shore entry also possible at Piti Pier for snorkeling and shallow diving.
notes: Protected marine preserve with restricted access - check current regulations with local dive operators. Shallow site suitable for beginners; natural freshwater percolation pits create unique water stratification. Excellent for photography and macro diving.

name: Pedra Pinnacle
description: Deep rock pinnacle rising from the seafloor with jagged formations and overhangs. Excellent for advanced divers seeking encounters with large barracuda schools, moray eels, octopuses in rocky crevices, and nurse sharks patrolling the bottom. Rock formations create dramatic visual relief and diverse microhabitats.
getThere: Fly to São Tomé International Airport (TMS). Boat transfers from Atlantic Diving Center or Dive São Tomé (15-20 minute ride).
